source_locator: Malware Choices Possibly Reflect Distinct APT29 Subteams; opening paragraph
attribution: APT29 attribution by Mandiant; confidence not stated for this observation
observation: Mandiant identified at least six distinct downloaders in APT29 diplomatic-focused activity during the first half of 2023.
interpretation: The group maintained several later-stage options; the report does not establish the internal development workflow.

corroboration.note: An independently observed, overlapping diplomatic campaign used multiple tools and versions. It does not verify Mandiant's count of six downloaders.

source_locator: March 2023: Earthquake-Themed Türkiye Campaign; both waves and Figure 3
attribution: APT29 attribution by Mandiant; confidence not stated for this observation
observation: In the early March Türkiye campaign, Mandiant documented ROOTSAW checking the client environment before follow-on delivery.
interpretation: Conditional delivery is adaptation to target context, but the report does not describe an AI model making that choice.

corroboration.note: The overlapping diplomatic campaign included environment assessment and manual verification after a different downloader. It does not independently verify this ROOTSAW behavior.

source_locator: March 2023: European Diplomatic-Focused Phishing Campaigns; opening paragraph and first wave
attribution: APT29 attribution by Mandiant; confidence not stated for this observation
observation: Mandiant reported two further ROOTSAW variants within roughly two weeks of the Türkiye campaign, moving newly added guardrails to the server side.
interpretation: The change shows a revised delivery design over a short campaign interval; it does not establish autonomous on-host mutation.

corroboration.note: The independent report describes several evolving tools in overlapping diplomatic activity, but does not verify the specific server-side ROOTSAW shift.

source_locator: July 2023: ICEBEAT Campaign; opening paragraph and first bullet
attribution: APT29 attribution by Mandiant; confidence not stated for this observation
observation: Mandiant reported a July 2023 PDF-based ROOTSAW delivery method and a new ICEBEAT downloader.
interpretation: This supports campaign-level iteration of the delivery chain, not autonomous on-host code revision.

corroboration.note: EclecticIQ and Mandiant list the same malicious PDF (MD5 fc53c75289309ffb7f65a3513e7519eb) and later binary (MD5 0be11b4f34ede748892ea49e473d82db). EclecticIQ calls that binary a Duke variant; Mandiant calls it ICEBEAT. The artifacts and chain are corroborated, while the naming differs.

source_locator: Industroyer2; paragraphs on protocol scope, code similarity, and embedded configuration
attribution: Sandworm attribution assessed with high confidence by ESET
observation: ESET found code similarities with Industroyer, support for one industrial protocol, and a detailed configuration embedded in Industroyer2.
interpretation: The design appears tailored to a known industrial environment; ESET concluded a different target would require a new build.

corroboration.note: Dragos separately describes Industroyer2 as a reconfigured, trimmed-down CRASHOVERRIDE variant and associates it with its ELECTRUM cluster. It does not verify ESET's specific embedded-configuration finding.

source_locator: DynoWiper deployment chronology and Attribution sections
attribution: ESET assesses Sandworm involvement with medium confidence; CERT Polska finds Static Tundra infrastructure overlap and cannot conclusively establish Sandworm involvement.
observation: ESET reported three DynoWiper samples deployed on December 29, 2025 and inferred revised builds after the earlier attempts failed; the attempts did not achieve the intended destructive impact.
interpretation: CERT Polska analyzed four related sample files across sites and grouped them into two functional versions. The reports support repeated deployment and a build revision between attempts; they do not establish AI-assisted development or autonomous on-host mutation.

corroboration.note: The same incident and a revised attempt after EDR blocking are confirmed. CERT Polska's four files/two versions have a broader counting scope than ESET's three deployed samples. CERT Polska does not confirm ESET's Sandworm attribution and identifies Static Tundra infrastructure overlap.

source_locator: Experimental Malware Using Gemini for Self-Modification to Evade Detection; first six paragraphs
observation: GTIG examined experimental samples designed to request code changes from an LLM. In the sample it analyzed, the self-update function was commented out and compromise capability was not demonstrated.
interpretation: The architecture shows an intention to regenerate code, but not a verified, functioning self-updating malware deployment.

corroboration.note: CAIRN identifies the same GTIG-linked SHA-256 and reports file metadata, but its VirusTotal-metadata method does not demonstrate the self-overwrite behavior it asserts. Its PE-centered architecture differs from GTIG's VBScript self-rewrite description. No runtime trace or applied-revision pair is published.

source_locator: Code Development: C2 Development and Support for Obfuscation; APT41 paragraph
attribution: Activity associated with APT41 by GTIG
observation: GTIG reported APT41-associated Gemini use for code-development assistance in August 2025.
interpretation: This is evidence of AI in a development workflow, not evidence that deployed malware consulted a model at runtime.

source_locator: Outsourcing Functionality: HONESTCUE; opening four paragraphs
attribution: Not associated with an existing threat cluster by GTIG
observation: GTIG examined HONESTCUE samples that requested code from Gemini for a later execution stage.
interpretation: A runtime model call appears in the sampled design, but the report does not establish continuous autonomous adaptation in active operations.

source_locator: LLM Generating Commands to Steal Documents and System Information; first four paragraphs
attribution: GTIG identifies APT28; CERT-UA links the campaign to APT28 with moderate confidence
observation: GTIG reported APT28's use of PROMPTSTEAL, also called LAMEHUG, in live operations against Ukraine. The malware queries a hosted model for commands to carry out its document and system-information collection tasks.
interpretation: This is operational evidence for runtime model-generated commands. The described objectives remain fixed; the reports do not establish repeated self-rewriting or autonomous target selection by the malware.

corroboration.note: CERT-UA identified the same LAMEHUG campaign and reported LLM-based command generation. Its APT28 attribution is moderate confidence; the advisory does not quantify successful model calls or infections.

source_locator: PromptSpy's AI-powered functionality and PromptSpy overview; sample upload date
attribution: No tracked actor attribution in ESET report
observation: ESET analyzed PromptSpy samples uploaded in February 2026. In its analysis the Android malware used a model to interpret screen context and guide a multistep interaction; ESET had not seen the malware in its production telemetry.
interpretation: The analyzed sample shows context-sensitive runtime behavior, but the report does not verify real-world deployment or code self-modification.

corroboration.note: GTIG separately examined PromptSpy's model-guided interface loop and assessed it as extensible, but its report does not identify an exact shared sample by digest. The broader range of possible goals is an inference from the design, not observed field use.

source_locator: Opening findings, AI configuration, and Sample details (first seen date)
attribution: No tracked actor attribution in Talos report
observation: Talos analyzed a VOLTA sample first seen in October 2026 that includes an optional model-based victim-assessment stage after data collection, with alternate models if a response is refused.
interpretation: The sample delegates analysis of collected data to a model. The report does not give a victim count or establish that the model stage ran in a field infection, and the model does not revise the malware code.

source_locator: Introduction and The evolution of MATCHBOIL; telemetry sightings and version summary
attribution: ESET attributes the malware family to the Russia-aligned UAC-0099 group
observation: ESET found MATCHBOIL at Ukrainian organizations in several separated telemetry periods from July 2025 through June 2026. Comparing versions, it documented changes to obfuscation, persistence, sandbox checks, and execution cadence while the downloader's core task remained stable.
interpretation: This supports repeated development and deployment of revised builds, not an on-host program rewriting itself or an AI-assisted development claim. The interval brackets separate sightings, not continuous activity.

corroboration.note: CERT-UA independently investigated an August 2025 UAC-0099 campaign using MATCHBOIL and described the loader's purpose. It confirms operational family use but does not verify ESET's later version chronology or exact change list.

source_locator: Opening findings; Attribution and Victimology; AI-Generated Malware in 2026; CrystalShell and ZigShell sections
evidence_basis: incident artifacts, sample analysis, and project metadata
attribution: Bitdefender assesses the activity as APT36 with medium confidence
observation: Bitdefender reported parallel implants on identified victims and analyzed variants from late 2025 into February 2026. Recovered project metadata pointed to AI-integrated code editors; the researchers also documented implementation flaws in some components.
interpretation: The report supports AI-assisted, high-volume development and a diversified tool portfolio, with human-run intrusions. It does not show the deployed implants autonomously rewriting their code. The month range is bounded by reported variant activity, not a claim of uninterrupted deployment.

source_locator: Opening findings; How SilkParasite Was Found; AI-assisted development discussion
evidence_basis: incident investigation, sample analysis, and operator artifacts
attribution: Bitdefender assesses a China-nexus cluster with medium confidence and does not assign a named group
observation: An October 2025 infection led Bitdefender to identify seven remote-access tool families in the operation. The researchers assessed AI-assisted development at medium confidence from code and artifact clues, while treating the precise group identity as unresolved.
interpretation: The case illustrates a maintained modular portfolio and an inferred developer-assistance role for AI. It does not establish runtime model calls or autonomous code changes in deployed implants.
